newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market little surprised by rate hikes.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market little surprised by rate hikes.

text.p: Dutch money market dealers were little surprised by today's move of the Dutch central bank to raise both the special advances rate and the secured loans rate.

"These are the so-called give-aways; everybody could see what the guilder was doing versus the mark, and given the circumstances, the Dutch central bank could nothing else but roll out the big guns," one dealer said.
He added the only surprise was the fact the rise in the secured loans rate was 0.50 instead of 0.25 percent.
"The money market had been anticipating a hike in both rates, but the move in the secured loans was 0.25 percent bigger than expected," another dealer agreed.
He said this was a way for the central bank to give itself some extra leeway for a possible downward correction later on.
Money market rates edged a few basis points higher in a reaction to the announcement of the rate hikes, with call money quoted 3.00 percent bid versus 2.93 earlier during the day.
"It was already more or less included in money market rates," one dealer said, adding trade was not particularly brisk.
The guilder hardly moved after the rates rise.
A spokesman for the Dutch central bank said the rate hikes had been prompted by standard monetary policy to keep the guilder rate in line with that of the mark.
The Dutch central bank said this afternoon it raised its special advances rate by 0.20 percent to 2.90 percent, while the secured loans rate was raised 50 basis points to 2.50 percent.

The special advances rate was raised 20 basis points to 2.70 percent on February 27, while the secured loans rate - the equivalent of Germany's discount rate - had been pegged at 2.00 percent since April 1996.
